title: Every Switch Costs You Time
action: One task, one visible timer
caveats: Re-verified by search: 4 lab experiments; cost rose with rule complexity and shrank with cues. Lab tasks only. Matches idea.md.

title: Could Your Bedtime Screen Keep You Up?
action: Dim lights, paper not screen
verified_source: Chang, Aeschbach, Duffy & Czeisler 2015, PNAS 112(4), 1232-1237 (doi:10.1073/pnas.1418490112)
caveats: Re-verified. NEW detail found: n = 12 adults, 2-week lab study, so an 'n = 12' limit can now be stated (read the paper to confirm). Also found: less REM and lower melatonin.

title: Do You Need Motivation to Start?
action: Fixed cue + tiny start
caveats: Re-verified. Six studies; largely correlational and self-reported, as the card says. The N = 2,274 total was not in my search snippets: it is in idea.md from the abstract. Free full text is on PMC if you want to confirm.

title: Does a Visible Savings Goal Help?
action: Name and show the goal
verified_source: Soman & Cheema 2011, J. Marketing Research 48(SPL), S14-S22 (doi:10.1509/jmkr.48.spl.s14)
caveats: Paper confirmed. Participants were low-income construction laborers in rural India, savings goal in envelopes (single vs split in two; children's photo on envelope as the reminder). Check that the video does not imply jars/coins or US consumers. Full PDF is free.

title: Does Automatic Saving Beat Willpower?
action: Schedule a tiny auto-transfer
caveats: Re-verified: one large US company; participation higher under auto-enrollment; many kept the default rate. NBER working paper is free.

title: Is Hitting Snooze Really That Bad?
action: Try the snooze or skip it on purpose
verified_source: Sundelin, Landry & Axelsson 2023, J. Sleep Research (doi:10.1111/jsr.14054)
caveats: Re-verified: Study 1 n = 1,732 (69% snooze at least sometimes); Study 2 n = 31 lab; 30 min snoozing improved or did not affect cognition on waking; about 6 min sleep lost. Only one 30-min snooze tested. Link above is a news summary, not the paper.

title: Build an Emergency Kit, One Item per Payday
action: Add 1 gallon of water to the list
verified_source: Hiatt et al. 2022, Disaster Med Public Health Prep 16(3), 1029-1037 (doi:10.1017/dmp.2020.480)
caveats: Re-verified: n = 572, fielded Aug 2014, 53% met FEMA's 3-day water guidance. The 96% food figure did NOT appear in my search results: confirm it in the abstract before publishing. Ready.gov water wording still to confirm.

title: Phone Screen Time: What the Research Says
source_type: Experimental studies on phone presence / use
action: Move the phone out of the room for one work block
guardrail: Replications mixed; say so in limit line
verified_source: Ward et al. 2017, 'Brain Drain', J. Assoc. Consumer Research (doi:10.1086/691462); replications: Ruiz Pardo & Minda 2022, Acta Psychologica; Hartmann et al. 2021
caveats: Original effect FAILED to replicate in pre-registered attempts. Do not claim 'phone in view drains focus'. Reframe as a myth check or pick different evidence.

title: Beating 'I'll Start Tomorrow'
action: Do the first 2 minutes only
verified_source: Steel 2007, Psychological Bulletin 133(1), 65-94 (doi:10.1037/0033-2909.133.1.65); 691 correlations
caveats: Supports task aversiveness, delay, impulsiveness as predictors. Does NOT support the 'do 2 minutes' fix: that step needs its own source or is labelled a suggestion.

title: Power Outage Hacks That Actually Matter
action: Test your flashlight and batteries
verified_source: Ready.gov power-outage page (kit: flashlights, extra batteries; use flashlights not candles; discard food above 40F for 2+ h)
caveats: Live page not fetched; wording seen via mirrors. Re-read the live page before scripting.

title: Save More Tomorrow: Commit Part of Your Next Raise
origin: Added 2026-11-08, no trend data - Replaces lifestyle creep
action: Decide today what share of your next raise goes to savings
verified_source: Thaler & Benartzi 2004, Journal of Political Economy 112(S1), S164-S187 (doi:10.1086/380085): 78% of those offered joined; 80% stayed through 4th raise; saving rate 3.5% to 13.6% over 40 months
caveats: Figures from the abstract; first implementation at one mid-size firm. Not a recommendation of any rate. Replaces the unsourced lifestyle-creep topic with a tested version of the same idea.

title: A Penny That Doubles vs $1 Million
action: Compute your own doubling table
verified_source: SEC Investor.gov compound interest calculator (tool, not a study); doubling is plain arithmetic
caveats: Calculator page confirmed to exist; label as illustrative math.

title: Could You Cover a Surprise Bill?
action: Open a separate 'surprise' bucket
verified_source: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2024 (SHED), published 2025-05-28: 63% would cover a $400 expense with cash or equivalent
caveats: A 2025 edition is probably out (May 2026): check for the latest figure. Fed notes some who would not use cash still have access to $400.

title: The Fresh Start Effect: Why Mondays Feel Like a Reset
origin: Added 2026-11-08, no trend data - Replaces 1% better
action: Pick the next Monday or the 1st and start one tiny habit then
guardrail: Say 'in archival data'; no causal claim beyond the paper
verified_source: Dai, Milkman & Riis 2014, Management Science 60(10), 2563-2582: searches for 'diet', gym visits and goal commitments rose after temporal landmarks (new week, month, year, birthday)
caveats: Archival field data (Google searches, gym check-ins, a goal site), not an experiment on habit success. Full PDF on Wharton faculty site.

title: The 24-Hour Rule for Impulse Buys
action: Put one cart item on a 24 h hold
guardrail: No % claim unless a study gives it
verified_source: Moser, Schoenebeck & Resnick, impulse-buying delay experiments (U. Michigan Deep Blue): 25 h delay lowered urge and purchase intent; 10 min delay did not
caveats: Dissertation-linked dataset, not a published journal paper (find the published version). Measures urge/intent, not regret or money saved. Do not claim a % reduction.

title: Japanese Walking: Interval Walking Explained
action: 3 min fast / 3 min easy, repeat
guardrail: NMA; ask a clinician if you have a condition
verified_source: Nemoto, Gen-No, Masuki, Okazaki & Nose 2007, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 82(7), 803-811 (doi:10.4065/82.7.803); RCT, 246 adults, mean age 63
caveats: Correct the queue source: first author is Nemoto, not Masuki. Participants were middle-aged/older: do not generalize to students. Outcome was BP, strength, aerobic capacity. Interval protocol: 3 min at 70% / 3 min at 40% peak capacity.

title: The 10-Minute Walk After Meals
source_type: Post-meal walking and blood glucose studies
action: Walk 10 min after one meal
verified_source: Buffey et al. 2022, Sports Medicine 52, 1765-1787 (doi:10.1007/s40279-022-01649-4): light walking breaks lowered post-meal glucose vs sitting (7 acute studies)
caveats: Breaks were 2-5 min every 20-30 min, not '10 min after meals'. Short-term biomarkers only; no diabetes outcomes. Rephrase the claim to match.

title: "21 Days to Form a Habit"?
action: Track one habit for 1 day
verified_source: Lally, van Jaarsveld, Potts & Wardle 2010, European J. Social Psychology (doi:10.1002/ejsp.674): median 66 days to plateau, range 18-254
caveats: n = 96 students, 84-day study; the 254 days is a model projection, only some fit well. State these limits. 21 days is not from this study.

title: The If-Then Plan
action: Write one 'If [cue], then I will [habit]'
verified_source: Gollwitzer & Sheeran 2006, Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 38, 69-119: d = .65 across 94 tests
caveats: A 2024 meta-analysis (Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer, 642 tests) found smaller bias-corrected effects (d about 0.15-0.35). Cite both or use the newer one.

title: Does Paying Cash Hurt More Than Card?
origin: Added 2026-11-08, no trend data - Replaces subscription audit
action: Pay for one purchase with cash and notice how it feels
guardrail: NFA; no card or bank advice
verified_source: Prelec & Simester 2001, 'Always Leave Home Without It', Marketing Letters 12(1), 5-12: bids to pay were higher when told payment would be by credit card than by cash
caveats: Lab auction with students (check n and sample in the full text). The MIT faculty page lists a different title: use the Springer record. Not a claim about real-world overspending.

title: $5 a Day for 10 Years = ?
action: Write down one daily spend and its yearly total
verified_source: SEC Investor.gov compound interest calculator (tool); arithmetic
caveats: Label illustrative, state the assumed rate.

title: Same Wake-Up Time, Even on Weekends
action: Set one alarm for the same time tomorrow
verified_source: Archived CDC sleep-hygiene page (2012): same bedtime/wake time each day, credited to National Sleep Foundation
caveats: No current CDC page confirmed and 'including weekends' not verified at CDC. Find a sleep-regularity study or current CDC/NIH page.

title: Morning Light and Your Body Clock
action: Step outside for 10 min after waking
verified_source: NIH/PMC literature: morning light advances the circadian clock (e.g. PMC4830627, PMC4344919); not individually read
caveats: Only abstracts/snippets seen. Pick one specific paper and read it; effect sizes unknown. Mostly small studies.

title: Is Your Evening Coffee Hurting Your Sleep?
action: Move the last coffee 2 hours earlier
verified_source: Drake, Roehrs, Shambroom & Roth 2013, J. Clinical Sleep Medicine 9(11), 1195-1200 (doi:10.5664/jcsm.3170)
caveats: n = 12 healthy sleepers, 400 mg caffeine, effect at 0, 3 and 6 h before bed. Participants did not notice the disruption. The 'after 5 p.m.' cutoff is press, not the paper.

title: Temptation Bundling: Pair a Want With a Should
origin: Added 2026-11-08, no trend data - Replaces habit stacking
action: Save one show or podcast for only while you do a chore
guardrail: Say 'in one study'; effect faded in later weeks
verified_source: Milkman, Minson & Volpp 2014, Management Science 60(2), 283-299 (doi:10.1287/mnsc.2013.1784; PMID 25843979): audiobooks available only at the gym
caveats: 226 participants over 10 weeks, and a '51% more gym visits' figure appeared in secondary sources only: read the paper before using any number. I recall the effect fading after a Thanksgiving break (unverified).

title: The 5-Minute Smoke Alarm Check
source_type: U.S. Fire Administration / NFPA / Ready.gov guidance
action: Press the test button on one alarm
verified_source: Fire-department and state fire-marshal pages repeating NFPA: test alarms monthly, replace every 10 years
caveats: Primary NFPA / USFA page not retrieved. Cite nfpa.org or usfa.fema.gov after reading it.

title: Your Two Ways Out: A 5-Minute Home Plan
action: Name two exits for one room
verified_source: NFPA-derived guidance: mark two ways out of each room; practice twice a year
caveats: 'If possible' qualifier common. Primary NFPA page not retrieved: cite after reading.

title: Lock Your Savings Away: A Commitment Account Study
origin: Added 2026-11-08, no trend data - Replaces sinking funds
source_type: Ashraf, Karlan & Yin 2006, Quarterly Journal of Economics
action: Name one goal and put a date on it
guardrail: NFA; no bank or product picks
verified_source: Ashraf, Karlan & Yin 2006, QJE 121(2), 635-672 (doi:10.1162/qjec.2006.121.2.635): randomized offer of a commitment savings account at a Philippine bank; 28.4% of 710 offered opened it; savings rose versus controls
caveats: Philippines bank customers; only the abstract was read. Overlaps episode 05 (automatic saving): angle is self-chosen restriction. Avoid quoting the 81-point figure without the full text.

title: The 5-Minute Monthly Blackout Check
action: Test your flashlight and batteries
verified_source: Ready.gov power-outage / kit guidance (flashlights, extra batteries)
caveats: Same as Power Outage Hacks. Overlaps that topic: consider merging.

title: Sign Up for Local Emergency Alerts in 5 Minutes
action: Search your county name + emergency alerts and sign up
verified_source: Ready.gov 'Know Your Alerts and Warnings' handout: confirm phone gets Wireless Emergency Alerts; sign up for local opt-in text/email alerts; consider NOAA Weather Radio
caveats: Ready.gov has no single sign-up page: search 'county name + emergency alerts'. WEA needs no sign-up. Ready.gov page noted as under revision: re-check.
